title: Fixed site-size counts did not identify site groups from pair response laws in three selected adult worm circuits
abstract: We tested whether fixed site-size counts remove ambiguity in target groups at synaptic sites. We used 95 source circuits with three through eight retained targets in two adult C. elegans maps. An integer search found exact alternatives in three circuits with site-size counts fixed, compared with four circuits when sizes were free. Each fixed-size alternative kept the source site count, every target count and every pair shared-site count. Under equal independent Bernoulli release and unit target gains, every pair response law is then equal for every release probability. Three-target silence differed. Independent integer checks passed for all witnesses. At assumed release probability 0.2, the largest triple silence difference in each fixed-size witness ranged from 0.010995 to 0.052429. These are model examples, not measured release effects or optimized bounds. Selected circuits, two animals, unknown source annotation error and strong release assumptions limit the result. The alternatives need not preserve geometry or physical site identity. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and pinned external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Checked alternatives with free and fixed target counts per site in 48 selected circuits from adult map 7 and 47 from adult map 8. Counts describe a release model, not measured neural activity.
